facts.statement: Streptospondylus is a genus of megalosaurid theropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of France, approximately 161 million years old.
facts.quote: Streptospondylus, (Ancient Greek στρεπτός (streptós), meaning "twisted", and σπόνδυλος (spóndulos), meaning "vertebra",) is a genus of megalosaurid theropod dinosaur known from the Late Jurassic period of France, 161 million years ago.

facts.statement: This predator was medium-sized, with an estimated length of 6 meters and a weight of 500 kilograms.
facts.quote: It was a medium-sized predator with an estimated length of 6 meters (19.5 ft) and a weight of 500 kg (1,100 lbs).

facts.statement: Georges Cuvier scientifically described theropod vertebrae in 1808 as the first dinosaur remains ever, though he initially misidentified them as crocodilian.
facts.quote: In 1808, Cuvier scientifically described the theropod vertebrae as the first dinosaur remains ever.

facts.statement: Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer renamed Steneosaurus rostromajor as Streptospondylus altdorfensis in 1832, referring the theropod remains to it.
facts.quote: In 1832 however, the German paleontologist Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer split the material. Steneosaurus rostrominor was renamed Metriorhynchus geoffroyii while Steneosaurus rostromajor became Streptospondylus altdorfensis.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the vertebrae being opisthocoel, meaning convex in front and concave behind, unlike typical crocodile elements.
facts.quote: The genus name comes from Ancient Greek στρεπτός (streptós), meaning "twisted", and σπόνδυλος (spóndulos), meaning "vertebra", alluding to the fact that the vertebrae differed from typical crocodile elements in being opisthocoel: convex in front and concave behind.

facts.statement: Streptospondylus was earlier assigned to crocodilian groups in the 19th century and typically classified in the Megalosauridae in the 20th century.
facts.quote: Earlier Streptospondylus assigned to crocodilian groups, in 19th century, in 20th century typically classified in the Megalosauridae.

facts.statement: A 2010 cladistic analysis indicated that Streptospondylus was the sister species of Magnosaurus within the Megalosauridae.
facts.quote: Later cladistic analysis by Benson and colleagues from 2010 indicated that Streptospondylus was the sister species of Magnosaurus within the Megalosauridae.

facts.statement: Carrano et al. placed Streptospondylus at Megalosauria incertae sedis in 2012 due to its fragmentary nature.
facts.quote: Carrano et al. (2012) placed Streptospondylus at Megalosauria incertae sedis due to its fragmentary nature.

facts.statement: Streptospondylus lived during the Callovian to Oxfordian stages, from 165.3 to 159 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Oxfordian (165.3 to 159 million years ago)

facts.statement: Streptospondylus is diagnosed by the unique bifurcation of the hypapophyses in the anterior dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Streptospondylus has been diagnosed by the unique bifurcation (split) of the hypapophyses (processes which extend from the lower surface of a vertebra) in the anterior dorsal vertebrae.

facts.statement: The theropod vertebrae of Streptospondylus were scientifically described in 1808 as the first dinosaur remains ever.
facts.quote: In 1808, Cuvier scientifically described the theropod vertebrae as the first dinosaur remains ever.
